topics.title: Capital, valuation and IPO
topics.one_liner: Series H priced Anthropic at $965B on May 28. The reported $2T IPO target is 2.1x that and 31x gross run-rate, yet no public S-1 exists.

key_metrics.label: Last priced round
key_metrics.value: Series H, May 28 2026: $65B at $965B post-money ($900B pre, derived). About $50B new cash plus $15B of earlier hyperscaler commitments (T1).

key_metrics.label: Total raised, equity-only (PitchBook basis, Sep 30)
key_metrics.value: $124.3B equity = A $124M + B $980M + C $450M + Google $2.0B + D $1.2B + Amazon notes $8.0B + E $3.5B + F $13B + G $30B + H $65B (PitchBook rows). $126.8B with the $2.5B May 2025 revolver. Press and T1 sizes give $123.4B. The Jul 16 figure of $161.3B wrongly added $34.5B of lessor SPV notes.

key_metrics.label: Latest reported IPO target (unconfirmed)
key_metrics.value: About $2T on Nasdaq. Raise up to $100B (WSJ, Sep 18, T3) versus at least $130B (The Information, Sep 3, T4). Timing November versus October is DISPUTED. No public S-1 on EDGAR at Sep 30.

key_metrics.label: Cash balance (press-reported, leaked draft prospectus)
key_metrics.value: $20.28B of cash, equivalents and short-term investments at Dec 31 2025 (Reuters, T2). No later balance is in the record, although about $95B of equity arrived in 2026.

key_metrics.label: Price over gross run-rate at each reference price (EV not computable)
key_metrics.value: Series H $965B is 20.5x (derived) on the $47B May run-rate and 14.8x on $65B at end-July. On $65B, secondary $1.2T to $1.5T is 18.5x to 23.1x and the $2T target 30.8x. Equity value, not EV: no net cash after Dec 31 2025 is in the record, and each $10B moves Series H by 0.2x.

what.t: Early ladder. Series A, May 2021: $124M, Tallinn lead, $461M post. Series B, Apr 2022: $580M per Anthropic (T1) but $980M per PitchBook, $3.0B post, FTX lead. Series C, May 2023: $450M, $4.55B post, Spark lead. Series D, 2024: $750M at $18.4B post per press (T2, T3) versus $1.2B at $21.0B per PitchBook, Menlo lead. Post-money for A to D is PitchBook or press; Anthropic published none.

Late ladder, Anthropic-announced (T1). Series E, Mar 3 2025: $3.5B at $61.5B post, Lightspeed lead. Series F, Sep 2 2025: $13B at $183B, ICONIQ lead. Series G, Feb 12 2026: $30B at $380B, GIC and Coatue lead. Series H, May 28 2026: $65B at $965B, led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia, with about $50B new cash and $15B of earlier hyperscaler commitments. Pre-money is post minus raise.

PitchBook's Sep 30 ledger (T2) shows $124.3B equity and $126.8B with the $2.5B May 2025 revolver, committed, draws undisclosed (T3). Its Jul 16 total of $161.3B counted $34.5B of chip-lease notes, since dropped without a stated reason. Press and T1 sizes sum to $123.4B, $850M lower, from Series B and D. A $15B pre-IPO revolver, 17 banks, reported near final (Bloomberg, Sep 3, T2), is not in the ledger.

Amazon's 10-Q (Jul 31, T1) shows $18.0B funded: $8.0B of notes plus $5.0B each of Series G and H preferred, carried at $190.4B, with $15.0B of a $20.0B milestone-gated facility left. Google had over $3B invested by Mar 2025 (DOJ filings, T2) plus up to $40B: $10B now, $30B on targets. Microsoft up to $5B, NVIDIA up to $10B and AMD up to $5B have no filed funded amounts.

Secondary marks are not priced rounds. FTX's estate sold 29.47M shares at $30.0045 in Mar 2024 (T1 court notice), the Series D price, with no cash to Anthropic. The May 2025 buyback ran at $56.09 and a Feb 2026 tender was planned at $350B pre-money (T3). Indications of $1.2T (Jul 9), trades to $1.5T (T3) and perpetuals near $1.8T (T4) are thin. Anthropic voids unauthorized transfers (May 12, T2).

On Jun 1 Anthropic announced it had confidentially submitted a draft S-1 (T1). EDGAR showed no public S-1 on Sep 30. Reported, unconfirmed: Nasdaq, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, about $2T. Raise is DISPUTED: up to $100B (WSJ, T3) versus at least $130B (The Information, T4). Timing is DISPUTED: October (Quartz, Aug 13) versus November (WSJ, Sep 18). Lock-up unknown. One Class F share holds 50.1% of votes (Reuters, T2).

means.t: Derived step-ups (pre over prior post, notes excluded): F 2.8x, G 1.9x, H 2.4x on T1 marks; B 4.4x, C 1.4x, D 4.4x, E 2.8x on PitchBook, where press gives D 3.9x, E 3.2x. H followed G by 3.4 months, about 20x annualized. Gross run-rate rose 3.4x and post-money 2.5x from G to H, so the multiple fell from 27.1x to 20.5x. On $65B, secondary marks are 18.5x to 23.1x.

Press-reported from the leaked draft: year-end 2025 cash was $20.28B and the $42B FY2025 net loss held a $34B non-cash charge on financing that could become shares (Reuters, T2). Derived: equity raised per dollar of gross run-rate fell from 4.2x at Series G to 1.9x at end-July; it is 27.1x FY2025 recognized revenue and 3.8x H1 2026 annualized. The $95B raised in 2026 is 76% of all equity.

The chip-lease notes are lessor debt. Broadcom's AI XPV Platform SPV borrowed $34.5B from Apollo-led funds with Blackstone, buys TPU systems and leases them to Anthropic for five years (T2). Anthropic has no credit rating, so Broadcom backstops about $30B (T3). Anthropic's own liability is the lease stream: $161.2B of Broadcom-related leases inside $518B of commitments, about 80% non-cancelable (Reuters, T2 and T3).

Strategic money is vendor financing. Amazon's $20B facility opens as AWS delivers compute and runs 30 months past a liquidity event (10-Q, T1). Google's $30B needs performance targets (T2). AMD's $5B follows deployment milestones (Reuters, T2). Amazon's $18.0B funded cost sits beside $110B of AWS commitments, 6.1x derived (Reuters, T3). Suppliers also grant equity: Akamai's warrant for up to 5% at $111.33 (T1).

implications.t: Count capital one way. Base capital efficiency on PitchBook's $124.3B equity-only, checked against $123.4B on press sizes, never $161.3B. Secondaries are excluded. Count notes once at funded cost, never fair value: Amazon $8.0B, while Google's $2.0B may undercount. Treat 'up to' amounts as zero until a filing shows cash, up to $65B here. Keep four $15B items apart: Microsoft-NVIDIA cap, Series H hyperscaler money, Amazon's facility, the revolver.

Price the IPO on basis. The $2T target is 2.1x the last priced round and above every reported mark. Derived multiples: 43.5x Q2 recognized revenue annualized, 30.8x gross run-rate, 18.2x a $110B year-end view, 10.3x bankers' $195B FY2028. Net of a 6% to 10% platform share it is 32.7x to 34.2x (PitchBook, T3). A $100B to $130B raise is 1.2x to 1.5x SpaceX's $86.2B record.

Build EV from commitments, not equity. $161.2B of leases sit outside the $124.3B equity line, and Amazon's unconverted notes carry at $97.9B fair value against a funded cost inside it. Net cash after Dec 31 2025 is not in the record. At end-2025 cash was 0.37x of $54.6B non-cancelable hosting commitments (derived, T3). Ask the S-1 for cash, revolver draws, lease liabilities and note carrying value first.

Treat holder marks as echoes of Series H, not evidence: Amazon ($190.4B), Zoom and Salesforce re-marked to the May 28 round; Alphabet and Microsoft gains fit it (inference). Amazon's stake is 15% to 20% (TheStreet, T3) or 21% (Forkast, T4); no filing states it. Its notes convert to nonvoting common at IPO, capped (10-Q, T1). A $2T print would lift its carrying value to about $395B (derived).

second_order: Public holders re-mark to Anthropic's price. Amazon took $62.8B of upward adjustments in H1 2026, Alphabet remeasured $87.9B of non-marketable stakes in Q2 with Anthropic unnamed, and Microsoft booked $3.2B. The record shows only upward adjustments so far. Their auditors and sell-side must react first if a priced IPO lands below $965B, the first observable down-mark. Consensus treats the $2T ask as one-way upside.

Lease-backed debt is the financing that scales. A second SPV package of about $36B was pitched Aug 5 and is not agreed (T3); the $71B 'stacked' headline adds it to the closed $34.5B. Google is exposed to up to $44B and Broadcom about $30B, so Broadcom and Google backstops stand in for Anthropic's missing rating and Apollo and Blackstone hold the risk behind them. Consensus counts $34.5B; the lease line is $161.2B, 4.7x larger (derived). A post-IPO rating push is headline-only (open item).

IPO proceeds are a small part of the bill. $100B to $130B is 19% to 25% of the $518B commitments and 24% to 31% of the roughly $414B non-cancelable part (derived). This extends the absorption thesis: the book is asked for $100B now and more financing follows. Consensus reads the IPO as the funding event. The payment schedule is not in the record, so the post-IPO gap cannot be sized.

OpenAI's exit from 2026 changes the comparable. Altman said 'not 2026' (Sep 13, T3) and Bloomberg has OpenAI seeking at least $30B at about $1.4T privately (Sep 29, T3), above Anthropic's $965B mark. Anthropic would list alone, so scarcity competes with absorption. The $2T target is 1.43x OpenAI's ask (derived). OpenAI's run-rate is $40B (Bloomberg) or $70B (Axios), so that ask is 35x or 20x.

Equity flows both ways. Akamai gave Anthropic a warrant for up to 5% at $111.33 and RUM's $0.01 warrants cover 50.8M shares (T3), while NVIDIA is reported weighing a $10B anchor, 0.5% at $2T (T3). Underwriters face related-party questions, the price-sensitive float is smaller than the headline raise, and Class A buyers get one vote a share against Class F's 50.1%. No filing traces cash from an investment to a supplier invoice.

watch.item: Public S-1 on EDGAR with price range, share count and selling holders
watch.threshold: SpaceX went from draft to public S-1 in 51 days and from public S-1 to listing in 23. Anthropic is at 121 days. A public S-1 after Oct 23 leaves a mid-November debut short of SpaceX's 23-day gap; after Nov 7 even Nov 30 runs faster.

watch.item: Roadshow launch, price range and raise size
watch.threshold: Reuters via Forbes (T3) put the roadshow no earlier than mid-October. A raise above $100B supports The Information's $130B. At or below $86.2B matches SpaceX's record with over-allotment. A range implying under $965B post-money is a down mark against Series H; one near $2T confirms the reported target.

watch.item: Lock-up length, selling holders and 10b5-1 plans in the public S-1
watch.threshold: 180 days or less versus the longer terms The Information reported (T4). Any secondary component means primary proceeds fall below the headline raise. Employee 10b5-1 plans would confirm managed supply.

watch.item: Q3 2026 results and adjusted operating income before the debut
watch.threshold: WSJ says Q3 results come first. Revenue under about $16B, a quarter of $65B, would mean run-rate stalled after July. A second adjusted profit is expected (FT, T3); a GAAP bridge tests the above-80% adjusted gross margin against PitchBook's 44%.

watch.item: Holder filings for the quarter ended Sep 30: Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft
watch.threshold: Amazon's Anthropic carrying value versus $190.4B at Jun 30. Unchanged means no new observable price. Any fall is the first down-mark. Watch for a stated ownership percentage or the conversion cap, both absent today.

watch.item: Second chip-lease SPV package, about $36B pitched
watch.threshold: A close near $36B takes executed lessor debt to about $70B. Headlines that add pitched to closed debt, like the $71B one, overstate. Size, sponsor and structure were unsettled on Aug 5.

watch.item: Pre-IPO revolver terms: tenor, pricing, draws, and whether it replaces the $2.5B facility
watch.threshold: Capacity is $15B if it replaces the old facility and $17.5B if additive. A drawn balance before listing would signal liquidity use ahead of the raise.

watch.item: PitchBook Raised to Date after the next refresh
watch.threshold: Stays $126.754B. A return to $161.254B, or the $15B revolver added, changes the equity basis. Treating Amazon's two $5B purchases as add-ons would lift it by up to $10B.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the multiple went from 27.1x at Series G to 20.5x at H to 30.8x at the target on gross run-rate, and the $2T ask is 28x to 57x expected FY2026 revenue (28x on the desk-derived $72B, LOW; 57x on PitchBook's stale $35B) against Reuters' cited comps of Palantir 53x and SpaceX/Cloudflare 41.6x (T2), so the record cannot show multiples tracking quality. (b) Contradicts in size: the record's gross-to-net evidence is 7.6% (prospectus-implied, T3) and 6% to 10% (PitchBook, T3), so Series H was 21.8x to 22.8x net, below OpenAI's 34.1x to 35.5x March mark, and only the $2T target restores parity at 32.7x to 34.2x; the 39.75% haircut is not supported. (c) Extends: a $100B to $130B raise is 1.2x to 1.5x SpaceX's $86.2B record while OpenAI has shelved a 2026 IPO, but the $3.6T pipeline and historical annual IPO volume are not in the record. (d) Confirms the counting rule ($124.3B equity-only, notes counted once) and adds a limit: $161.2B of leases sit outside it and Amazon's notes are carried at $97.9B fair value, so $518B of commitments, about 8.0x run-rate, belongs beside CE. (e) Confirms: providers differ by $1B to $2B on 'raised', PitchBook carried lessor SPV notes as Anthropic debt until Sep 30, and the SpaceX playbook differs on insider selling (T4) and control, so its IPO template may not transfer.

uncertainties.note: No public S-1 exists. Cash of $20.28B, the $42B net loss with a $34B non-cash charge, $518B of commitments and the Class F terms come from a leaked draft that Reuters reviewed (T2), with relays at T3. The $15B revolver rests on Bloomberg and Forbes (T2, T3); tenor, pricing and draws are unknown.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A public S-1 with the capitalization table, contractual obligations table and credit agreement exhibit.

uncertainties.note: Equity raised is $124.3B (PitchBook), $123.4B (press and T1 sizes) or $113.5B without note money. Amazon's two $5B purchases, Google's $10B tranche and Microsoft and NVIDIA's 'portion' may sit inside G and H or beside them. PitchBook's G and H share fields are 2.55x and 2.57x round size. Primary versus secondary mix, and who funded the Feb 2026 tender and the $1.5B Bartz settlement, are not stated.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 capitalization table and a sources-and-uses statement.

uncertainties.note: Secondary marks from $1.05T to $1.8T are indications, SPV prints and perpetuals, not clearing prices. Binance's perpetual assumes 1B shares, while PitchBook's $589.01 Series H price implies about 1.64B fully diluted shares (derived, PitchBook-only price), so the $1.8T is a contract convention. The tender is 'up to $6B' in one headline and a '$60B pool' in another (T4).
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Executed trades with disclosed price and size, or the IPO book.

uncertainties.note: IPO size, price and date are unresolved. Reference class: four of four private rounds since Jan 2025 closed above the first reported size, by 1.3x to 3.0x from the top of each range. The record holds one mega-IPO precedent, SpaceX, so it has no IPO base rate. The reported date drifted from late September to after the midterms and two expected filing windows passed. What differs: float demand caps an IPO, a PBC with a Class F share is untested, and WSJ ties timing to Q3 results.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The public S-1 date, the price range and the Q3 print.

uncertainties.note: Desk tables are not clean ledgers. The capital table mixes talks, closed rounds and debt and sums to $199.4B; capital_summary is the ledger at $124.254B. The valuation table shows a $1.5T secondary mark at T2 and HIGH, and Series A and the $54B Amazon row at T1, though those valuations are PitchBook-only (T2).
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: desk-deals re-tiering the rows and removing talks from the capital table.

topics.title: Revenue, margins and customers
topics.one_liner: Q2 2026 revenue was $11.5B recognized, 14x YoY, but the $65B run-rate is gross and the record's 6-10% haircut evidence sits far below the desk's 39.75%.

key_metrics.label: Latest run-rate (outlet-reported)
key_metrics.value: $65B+ at end-July 2026, gross basis, 7.2x end-2025's $9B. Bloomberg via TechCrunch (T2), FT and Axios agree. Last company-stated figure: $47B in May (T1). Nothing above $65B is verified.

key_metrics.label: FY2025 recognized revenue
key_metrics.value: $4.59B, +1,088% YoY, gross of cloud resale. FY2024 about $0.39B, implied. Exit run-rates were $9B and $1B. Leaked draft prospectus via Reuters (T2), no public S-1.

key_metrics.label: Q2 2026 revenue
key_metrics.value: $11.5B recognized, 14x YoY and 2.4x Q1's $4.73B. H1 2026 is $16.2B. Leaked draft (T2). Beat the May 20 projection of $10.9B by 5.5%.

key_metrics.label: Gross margin, by definition
key_metrics.value: Above 80% adjusted, before partner share and training (FT, T3). About 40% for FY2025 (The Information, T3). About 44% for Q2 2026E (PitchBook, T3). No GAAP gross margin reported.

key_metrics.label: Channel share
key_metrics.value: 47% of FY2025 sales, $2.16B, through Amazon and Google marketplaces, up from 11% in 2023. Platforms kept about $351M, 7.6% of revenue (Reuters-computed, T3 in the prospectus table).

key_metrics.label: Customer concentration
key_metrics.value: Two unnamed customers at 12% each, about 24% of FY2025 revenue (T2). Most large customers lack long-term contracts (T3). The 1,000 customers above $1M floor only $1B, 1.5% of run-rate.

what.t: Run-rate path. Anthropic stated $9B at end-2025, $14B on Feb 12, above $30B on Apr 6 and above $47B in May (T1, gross basis inferred). Bloomberg via TechCrunch, Aug 17 (T2) reported above $65B at end-July, with FT and Axios agreeing. Nothing higher is verified. The $100B to $120B year-end figures from Quartz, FT, WSJ and the NYT via Gulf News (T4) are projections.

Recognized revenue. Reuters and Fortune read a leaked draft prospectus, Sep 28 to 29 (T2, single origin, no public S-1). The event is DISPUTED in the record because two periods share one field. FY2024 was near $0.39B, implied, and FY2025 $4.59B. Q1 2026 was $4.73B and Q2 $11.5B, 14x a year earlier. H1 2026 is $16.2B, 3.5x FY2025. The FY2025 operating loss was $8.06B, up from $2.98B.

Channel and customers. Reuters, Sep 29 (T3 in the prospectus table): Amazon and Google marketplaces carried 47% of FY2025 sales, $2.16B, up from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024. Anthropic books them gross as principal. Platforms kept about 16 cents per dollar, $351M, 7.6% of revenue. Two unnamed customers were 12% each. Most large customers lack long-term contracts.

Margins. Every figure has a different scope. The Information, Jan 21 (T3): FY2025 about 40%, below a 50% plan. FT, Sep 13 (T3): above 80% in Q2 2026 before partner share and training. PitchBook, Sep 16 (T3): about 44%. Adjusted operating income was positive in Q2 with no dollar amount. The $559M was a May 20 projection.

Mix. FY2025 revenue was $3.8B usage-based and $789M subscription, 17.2% (T2). Business was about 80% of sales (T4, Oct 2025). Claude Code run-rate rose from $1B in Nov 2025 to above $2.5B in Feb 2026, 18% of run-rate, no later figure (T1). Enterprise moved to a $20 seat plus API-rate usage (The Register, T2). Menlo, an Anthropic investor, gave Anthropic 54% of enterprise coding (T3).

Comparables. OpenAI's FY2025 revenue was $13.07B net of Microsoft share (T3) and its Q2 2026 $6.2B (WSJ via Proactive, basis unstated), against Anthropic's gross $11.5B. xAI booked $3.2B in FY2025 (T2). The 2028 plan went from $70B with $17B of cash flow (Nov 2025, T3, DISPUTED in the record for mixed fields) to $190B to $200B (Reuters, Aug 17, T2), with no cash-flow figure for the new plan.

means.t: A run-rate annualizes a recent period, so recognized revenue lags it in a fast ramp. FY2025 revenue was 0.51x the $9B exit run-rate and FY2024 was 0.39x. Desk-derived trailing revenue is about $19.6B, 0.30x of $65B (LOW). Growth is slowing: the pace fell from about $13B added a month from April to mid-May to about $7B a month since, 13.5% a month.

Anthropic books marketplace sales gross as principal, with the platform share in marketing expense. The haircut is take rate times channel share: 16 cents times 47% is 7.6%, and 16% at full share. A 39.75% haircut needs platforms to keep 85 cents per marketplace dollar and implies $4.6B paid away in Q2, against $1.9B forecast for all of 2026 (The Information, Feb). The record has no derivation.

Margins differ in scope. PitchBook's 44% equals one minus its projected $0.56 Q2 compute ratio ($0.71 in Q1), so it deducts only compute. The above-80% figure drops partner share and training. If $0.56 is all-in compute and inference is 37% of it, as The Information's 2026 plan implies, inference costs about $0.21 per dollar, near 80% (desk arithmetic). The ratio was $1.60 in FY2025.

Volume carries growth as prices fall. Sep 30 list prices per million tokens: Haiku $1/$5, Sonnet $2/$10, Opus $4/$20, Fable $10/$50. Opus fell 67% in Nov 2025 and 20% on Sep 22. A 20% cut needs 25% more tokens to hold revenue, a 67% cut needs 3x. Tokenizers add up to 35% more tokens, offsetting part of each cut. No volume series is in the record.

implications.t: Carry both haircuts until the S-1 fixes the basis. End-July net run-rate is $58.5B to $61.1B at 6% to 10%, and $39.2B at 39.75%. Applying the FY2025 fee ratio, Q2's $11.5B is 1.7x OpenAI's $6.2B (WSJ, basis unstated) at 7.6% and 1.1x at 39.75%. Do not plot the two labs' run-rates on one axis.

Label the denominator on every multiple. A reported $2T IPO target is 30.8x the gross end-July run-rate, 32.7x to 34.2x net of 6% to 10%, 43.5x Q2 annualized recognized revenue and about 10x the 2028 projection midpoint. Reuters' 18x to 20x states no revenue basis. Never apply a recognized-revenue multiple to run-rate.

Discount quality for concentration until names and terms appear. Two customers are about 24% of FY2025 revenue, and most large ones lack long-term contracts. Amazon and Google are investors, suppliers and the channel for 47% of sales. The 1,000 customers above $1M floor 1.5% of run-rate. Consumer grew an estimated 75% from January to mid-May, run-rate about 4x, so the 80% business split is stale.

Quote one margin only with its definition. Treat above 80% as a management view, 40% and 44% as estimates and GAAP gross margin as unreported. Score Q3 on a dollar amount for adjusted operating income and a GAAP bridge. Q2 had SpaceX's two-month discount, which a T5 relay of the WSJ says ended in July, with compute costs expected to rise in H2.

second_order: Bases will be forced into the open. If the S-1 keeps gross presentation, OpenAI and sell-side comps must bridge to net. If it moves to net, every run-rate print restates by the fee share. Either way Anthropic's $65B and OpenAI's nearly $70B (Axios, basis unstated, two months later) stop being comparable headlines. PitchBook already said neither company's basis would survive a Big Four audit.

The channel grows faster than the company. The Information projected partner payouts of $360M in 2025, $1.9B in 2026 and $6.4B in 2027, up 5.3x then 3.4x. Claude Platform on AWS and Foundry bill through marketplaces, so share likely rises above 47%, and cloud providers already collect 60% of receivables. The S-1 must explain a fee line that scales.

Price cuts make revenue depend on volume from coding agents. OpenAI answered Opus 5.5 the same day with Luna at $0.10 and $0.50, one-tenth of Haiku 4.5's $1 and $5. SpaceX, which sells Anthropic $1.25B a month of compute, agreed to buy Cursor, a named Claude coding customer. Distribution, rivalry and supply meet in one counterparty, and the record does not give Cursor's current share.

The valuation-quality gap is wider than the headlines. Recognized revenue is about 0.30x of run-rate, the run-rate is gross, and two margin figures differ by 36 points. Consensus is missing that the S-1 resets all three at once, and that the last verified run-rate is two months old in a business adding about $7B a month.

Comparable data need care. OpenAI's Q2 $6.2B with +18% QoQ (WSJ) implies Q1 of $5.25B, not the $5.7B in the record. xAI's Q2 AI-segment revenue includes compute rented to a customer the desk infers is Anthropic, so part of it is Anthropic's own cost. Neither series is a clean revenue comp.

watch.item: Next run-rate print after the $65B end-July figure, company-stated or from Bloomberg, FT or Axios
watch.threshold: Below $79B at end-September is under the straight-line path to $100B at year-end. Above $87B is on the $120B path. Any figure above $100B before December would be the first actual, not a projection.

watch.item: Public S-1 income statement: audited FY2025, H1 2026, cost of revenue, gross profit and the revenue-recognition note
watch.threshold: GAAP gross margin against above 80% adjusted and 40% to 44% estimates. GAAP operating result against the adjusted figure. Any move to net presentation or a stated principal-versus-agent policy change.

watch.item: Q3 2026 results, which WSJ says Anthropic will show investors before a November listing
watch.threshold: Revenue near $17B to $18B is on the path to $100B to $120B. $20B or more runs ahead. Under $16B means the run-rate stalled after July. Adjusted operating income positive a second quarter, with a dollar amount.

watch.item: S-1 channel data: marketplace share and platform fees for H1 2026, with Microsoft Foundry broken out
watch.threshold: Share above 47% or fees above 7.6% of revenue raises the record-based haircut. A fee ratio near 39.75% would be the first evidence for the canonical figure.

watch.item: S-1 customer note: names, shares and contract terms of the largest customers, and Cursor's weight after SpaceX's $60B purchase
watch.threshold: Any customer above 10% in H1 2026. The two 12% customers unchanged or named. Share of revenue under multiyear contracts.

watch.item: Haiku 5.5 list price, promised within weeks on Sep 28
watch.threshold: Below Haiku 4.5's $1/$5 extends deflation to the small tier, where OpenAI's Luna is $0.10/$0.50. An unchanged $1/$5 holds the floor.

watch.item: OpenAI Q3 2026 revenue and a stated basis, net of Microsoft share or not
watch.threshold: Q3 against $6.2B in Q2 and a run-rate nearing $70B. A stated net basis allows a like-for-like gap. Reconcile Q1 $5.7B with the +18% QoQ claim.

topics.one_liner: Only $217.9B of $592.1B in deals is firm on T1/T2 sources; 13.0 of 15.8 GW are 'up to'; about 80% of the $518B plan is non-cancelable.

key_metrics.value: Broadcom-related leases, $161.2B, 31% of the $518.2B named lines (T3). Google plus Broadcom lines are $272.3B, 52.5%. Amazon and Google also carried 47% of FY2025 sales, $2.16B (T3).

what.t: Compute desk tally, Sep 30 (desk arithmetic): $592.1B over 17 deal rows and 15.8 GW, of which 13.0 GW are 'up to' ceilings. Firm on T1/T2 evidence, $217.9B: Amazon, Microsoft, TeraWulf, Riot, RUM, Akamai, the SPV notes (Riot and RUM tenants are press-named). Cancellable or conditional, $89.6B: SpaceX, Nscale. Reported, unconfirmed, $46.8B: Lambda, Volta, Akamai plan 1. Prospectus coverage only, $237.8B: Google, Broadcom leases net of the SPV.

Reuters, Sep 28 to 29, on a leaked draft prospectus (T2 total, T3 split): at least $518B over about ten years with six partners, roughly 80% non-cancelable or payable regardless of use. Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, Microsoft $31.4B, Broadcom-related leases $161.2B, SpaceX up to $84.5B, AMD over $20B. Amazon and Google routed 47% of FY2025 sales (T3). Anthropic is shifting toward dedicated data centers and leased chips.

Vendor capital and compute owed (prospectus, T3). Amazon: $18.0B invested, $15.0B facility left (10-Q, Jul 31, T1), owed $110B. Google: up to $40B, $30B on targets (TechCrunch, Apr 24, T2), owed $111.1B. Microsoft up to $5B and Nvidia up to $10B (T1 caps), $30B Azure commitment (T1). AMD: up to $5B (T1), tied to deployment milestones (Reuters, T2), owed over $20B. Memory makers joined Series H (T1).

Financing, Jun 2 to Sep 3. Apollo and Blackstone closed $34.5B of SPV notes (A1 $6.0B, A2 $24.0B, B $4.5B) to buy Google TPUs leased to Anthropic for five years, over 1 GW, funded in about 16 stages, with Broadcom residual-value support (Quartz, T2). Blackstone pitched a second ~$36B (Bloomberg, Aug 5, T3). A $15B pre-IPO revolver, against $2.5B in 2025, is nearing final (Bloomberg, Sep 3, T2).

SpaceX, May 6 to Jul 9. Anthropic rents Colossus 1 (live since May, over 300 MW); the $1.25B monthly fee covers Colossus and Colossus II and is terminable by either side on 90 days' notice (SEC, T1). Musk says the firm period is 180 days (TechCrunch, T2). Prospectus coverage: up to $84.5B against $45B nominal (T3). SpaceX competes through Grok and is buying Cursor for $60B (8-K, T1).

Reuters, Sep 28 (T2): FY2025 compute and infrastructure spend was $7.33B, 58% of $12.65B operating expenses, on $4.59B revenue, $1.60 per $1. WSJ via PYMNTS, May 20 (T3): $0.71 in Q1 2026, $0.56 projected for Q2, scope unstated; Q2 revenue came in at $11.5B (Bloomberg, T3). FT, Sep 13 (T3): Q2 adjusted operating income positive; gross margin above 80% before partner share and training.

means.t: The three totals measure different things. The desk's $592.1B adds deal rows of mixed tiers. The Information's $517B is the maximum value of contracts signed since October 2025. The prospectus $518B is ten-year spend with six named partners. Bridge: $592.1B, less $144.8B of deals outside the six, plus $70.9B more on SpaceX, Amazon, Microsoft and AMD in the prospectus, is $518.2B. The 0.2% match with $517B is coincidence.

Fixed costs meet uncommitted revenue, with the same counterparties on both sides. Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Broadcom lines, described as must-pay or largely non-cancelable, sum to $413.7B, 79.8% of $518.2B. Amazon and Google hold 42.7% of the lines and routed 47% of FY2025 sales, while most large clients have no long-term contracts (T3). SpaceX, the flexible line, is cancelable by either side on 90 days' notice.

Capital follows delivery, and others carry the assets. Amazon's facility opens as AWS delivers (10-Q, T1), AMD's equity and Google's $30B gate on milestones or targets, and Nscale's order needs its financing. A lessor issues the TPU notes with Broadcom residual support and Theseus (Macquarie, GIC) funds data centers, so unrated Anthropic pays leases. No filing traces equity cash to a supplier invoice, so the loop is inferred.

The ratio fall reads as fixed-cost absorption, not proven cheaper tokens: Q1 growth ran 80x annualized against a 10x plan (Amodei, T3), so pre-bought capacity carried more revenue. List prices per token fell 73% on Opus and 33% on Sonnet, so at constant mix a revenue dollar needs more compute unless unit cost falls faster. No unit-cost series exists; 2025 cloud inference ran 23% over plan (T3).

implications.t: Reprice by bucket and basis. Firm T1/T2 is $217.9B; the prospectus non-cancelable core is $413.7B; never add them, The Information's $517B or the FT's ~$200B web. Treat 13.0 of 15.8 GW as options; three T1 statements put about 2.3 GW online by end-2026. Campus figures (Rainier 2.2 GW, Monarch 1.37 GW IT, SpaceX fleet 1.4 GW) are not Anthropic's share. Exclude talks and the $50B Fluidstack overlap.

Treat compute as step-fixed. Straight-line over ten years (no schedule exists), $518.2B is $51.8B a year, 80 cents per dollar of the $65B run-rate; the $413.7B core is 64 cents. Amodei says forecasting misses on compute bought years ahead are ruinous (T2). Do not extrapolate the 56-cent Q2 projection: Anthropic warned profit may not last the year, SpaceX's discount has likely lapsed and list prices have fallen.

Underwrite clusters, not logos. By chip class the desk tally is TPU 46%, NVIDIA GPUs 30%, Trainium 17%, other 7%; AMD is unpriced. Four chip families hedge chip risk, yet TPUs run through Google and Broadcom and Nvidia sits under six priced counterparties. Custom silicon is hiring only (T2). Nscale shows $2.6B active TCV against $103.4B contracted and a $1.02B H1 loss. Score delivery risk, not only credit.

Keep capital efficiency on equity only and show lease-financed capacity beside it. Equity raised is $124.254B. PitchBook's $126.754B includes the $2.5B revolver, and its Jul 16 total of $161.254B over-counted by the $34.5B of lessor notes. The $161.2B lease line and the $15B revolver never enter an equity denominator, so equity-only ratios flatter capacity that lessors finance.

second_order: Supplier backlogs lean on one customer. Nscale's $103.4B active-and-contracted TCV is 43% Anthropic by arithmetic, yet only $2.6B is active. The Information puts Anthropic above 40% of Google's disclosed backlog (T3, DISPUTED), and Broadcom's 8-K ties Anthropic's consumption to its commercial success. A thin S-1 commitment table could re-rate these suppliers before Anthropic. Google, Apollo, Blackstone and Nscale's IPO buyers must react.

Duration mismatch. Shell leases run 20 years (TeraWulf, Riot), GPU services six years (Nscale, Volta, RUM) and chip leases five years (SPV), so one shell spans four chip-lease cycles. Obsolescence and refinancing risk sit with Anthropic or its guarantors. Consensus counts gigawatts and dollars, not years.

The IPO is one leg of a larger financing stack. WSJ (T3) has up to $100B at about $2T, The Information (T4) at least $130B, while $34.5B of SPV notes closed in June, about $36B more is pitched and a $15B revolver is nearly final. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs appear as IPO leads, revolver leads and SPV note placers (T2 to T3). Ask the S-1 to show the fees and relationships.

The supply gap runs to 2027 and 2028, and power sets its pace. The draft prospectus expects demand to exceed supply (Reuters, T2). Shells energize from late 2027 (landlord dates; no slippage base rate in the record), so rented scarcity (about $8 to $12 per GPU-hour, desk-derived) and rate limits bridge it. Anthropic pledged to fund grid upgrades and ordered 470 MW of onsite generation from ERock (T1).

Milestone gating correlates failure. Amazon's facility, AMD's equity, Google's $30B and Nscale's financing all open on delivery or targets, so a delivery slip delays capital and capacity together, while a demand slip hits the non-cancelable core and the suppliers' equity marks at once: Amazon carries its stake at $190.4B against $18.0B invested. The usual critique is that circularity inflates demand. It also couples failures.

topics.one_liner: Opus list price fell 73% in under 14 months to $4/$20 as releases reached one per three weeks, yet nearly all benchmark evidence is Anthropic's own.

what.t: Anthropic (T1), Sep 22 and 28: Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per MTok, -20% vs Opus 5, cache reads $0.20, fast mode $8/$40. Sonnet 5.5 at unchanged $2/$10, half Opus 5.5's price. Anthropic claims 40% lower typical cost than Opus 5 and up to 30% lower cost per task for Sonnet 5.5. SiliconANGLE (T3, single source): OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 on Sep 22.

Price sheets and docs (T1). Flagship: Claude 2.x $11.02/$32.68 (launch price unverified) to $8/$24 (Nov 21 2023, -27%); Opus $15/$75 (Mar 2024) to $5/$25 (Nov 24 2025, -67%) to $4/$20 (Sep 22 2026, -20%). Mid: $3/$15 from Mar 2024 to $2/$10 (Jun 30 2026, -33%). Small: Haiku 3 $0.25/$1.25 to Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, a 4x rise. Restricted: Mythos Preview $25/$125 post-credit to Mythos 5 $10/$50 (Jun 9, -60%).

Pricing table (mostly T1 sources): 29 model rows on 23 release dates since Mar 14 2023, at 4, 5, 7 and 13 rows in 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 to date. Opus gaps since Nov 2025 ran 42 to 73 days. Haiku 4.5 (Oct 15 2025) has no successor, and TechCrunch (T2) said Sep 22 and Sep 28 that a new Haiku comes within weeks.

Anthropic (T1) disclosed Claude Code run-rate of over $500M (Sep 2 2025), $1B (Nov 2025) and over $2.5B (Feb 12 2026), with enterprise over half of it. Company run-rate was $14B on Feb 12. Cowork launched Jan 12 for Max (TechCrunch, T2), went GA Apr 9 and merged into Claude chat Sep 16. The Register (T2, Apr 16) reported Enterprise moved to $20 per seat plus API-rate usage.

Anthropic (T1): a US directive on Jun 12 2026 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5, and Anthropic disabled both for everyone. Commerce approved Mythos 5 for 100+ US institutions Jun 26 (Semafor, T2; MeriTalk: Jun 27). Controls lifted Jun 30; Fable 5 returned Jul 1. Mythos 5.1 is US-only, and on Sep 24 the White House asked Anthropic to hold it from UK AISI (Politico, T2).

Every benchmark score in the record from Claude 2 (Jul 2023) through Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28 2026) comes from Anthropic's own posts or coverage of them. The only independent data is one undated T3 snapshot fetched Sep 30. Artificial Analysis index: Opus 5.5 58, Sonnet 5.5 56, Fable 5.1 53, GPT-6 Astra 53. Arena agent win share: Fable 5.1 14.58%, Astra 11.78%, Opus 5.5 11.15%.

means.t: List price falls in steps at launches. Opus 5 claimed to beat Fable 5 at lower cost, and Opus 5.5 claims Fable 5.1 performance at 40% of its price. Effective price falls faster: cache reads are 10% of input, now 5% for Opus 5.5 and 2.5% for Fable 5.1; batch is 50% off; the fast-mode premium fell from 6x (VentureBeat, T2) to 2x.

Two forces run against deflation: Opus 4.7's tokenizer adds up to 35% more tokens per text at flat list price, and Haiku's price rose 4x. Revenue per token is a weak guide. Reported margin rose from about 50% for 2025E (The Information, T3) to above 80% adjusted for Q2 2026 (FT, T3, before partner share and training). Unit cost, mix or scope could explain it; no cost-per-token series exists.

Coding agents are heavy automated users: 79% of Claude Code conversations were automation versus 49% on Claude.ai (Anthropic, Apr 2025). Flat plans strain, so Anthropic added weekly limits (Aug 28 2025), API-rate usage credits for Fable and Enterprise seats at $20 plus metered usage. Chat still grows: paid consumer subscriptions more than doubled in early 2026 (T2). Revenue moves toward tokens times price, which exposes it to deflation.

Interpretation: a release every three weeks means overlapping training, post-training and safety work, so R&D runs continuously. The leaked prospectus (Reuters, T2) shows FY2025 opex of $12.65B on revenue of $4.6B, and compute infrastructure spend of $7.33B with no definition in the record. Earliest retirement dates for five current models sit 12 months after release. The $518B compute plan is about 80% non-cancelable (T3).

implications.t: Reprice revenue as tasks times price per task, not tokens times list price. Run-rate rose 7.2x from about $9B (end 2025) to over $65B (end July, T2) at mostly flat Opus and Sonnet list prices, so growth was volume and mix. The Sonnet 5 and Opus 5.5 cuts are the first test. No token or task series exists here. Ask the S-1 for tokens, price, mix and net revenue retention.

Treat the $10/$50 tier as next to reprice. Anthropic's Sep 22 table has Opus 5.5 ahead of Fable 5.1 on all six benchmarks that list both, at 40% of the price. Artificial Analysis (T3) scores Fable 5.1 lowest of three Claude models, and only Arena's agent ranking puts it first. Interpretation: a freeze costs general users the premium, since other models stayed up, but restricted users lack a substitute.

Price position: parity at the consumer and mid tiers, premium at the low end. Pro at $20 matched ChatGPT Plus (Sep 2023), Sonnet 5.5 at $2/$10 matches GPT-6 Sol, but Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 is 10x Luna (SiliconANGLE, T3, single source). Astra and Google prices are not in the record. Haiku 5.5 is the first small-tier price test since Oct 2025.

Discount vendor-only claims until independent data confirm them: SWE-bench Verified from 49.0% (Oct 2024) to 93.9% (Apr 2026), Terminal-Bench, GDPval-AA, per-task cost cuts and Glasswing's 10,000+ flaws (75 of 530 reported open-source bugs patched). Series are re-versioned at launches, and Fable 5's GDPval-AA reads 1932 on Jun 9 and 1723 on Sep 1. Tag each dashboard claim vendor or independent.

second_order: Basis: Anthropic books revenue gross of cloud resale, so each list cut lowers reported revenue one for one while the partner share sits in cost. The FT's above 80% gross margin excludes that share and training. OpenAI reports net. Interpretation: reading the cuts only as a margin issue misses the basis question, which decides how much of each cut shows in reported revenue.

Distribution: Cursor is named at several Claude launches and is being bought by SpaceX for $60B (8-K, Jun 16; no closing in the record). SpaceX/xAI also supplies Anthropic 300 MW at Colossus. A cheaper Opus helps Cursor's margin, but a channel owned by a rival and supplier can steer volume. Two unnamed customers were nearly 25% of 2025 revenue in the leaked prospectus.

Availability is now a policy variable. One letter cut the two frontier models for 19 days, Mythos 5.1 is US only, and the White House asked for a UK AISI hold. Anthropic pledged to work with Commerce on protocols for future models. The next Fable or Mythos release may carry review risk, and non-US buyers may get a lagging tier.

Limits are a second price lever that a list-price view misses. Anthropic doubled Claude Code five-hour limits on May 6 after renting Colossus and raised limits again with Opus 5.5. Each raise is a price cut to subscribers, and each tightening drew suits (Kahn, Patel). Deflation shows up in limits as well as list prices.

Pacing: releases did not slow after the CEO's Sep 12 essay urging a pace cap. Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 followed within 16 days, and the Buist antitrust suit cites the essay. The S-1 risk factors should reconcile a stated pacing stance with a three-week cadence.

watch.item: Haiku 5.5 launch and list price
watch.threshold: TechCrunch (T2) said 'coming weeks' on Sep 22 and Sep 28, and Haiku 4.5 is 350 days old. A price above $1/$5 extends the 4x small-tier rise. At or below $1/$5 defends volume against Luna at $0.10/$0.50.

watch.item: Independent benchmark updates for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (Artificial Analysis, Arena, Epoch), and first embedded-evaluator output
watch.threshold: Opus 5.5 holding 58 with Fable 5.1 at 53 supports the vendor ladder and the premium-tier risk. Arena already has Astra above Opus 5.5 at High effort; Astra still ahead at matched effort would contradict Anthropic's Terminal-Bench 4.0 gap of 66.4 vs 57.9. Faculty (named Sep 18, jointly funded) and METR output is only partly independent.

watch.item: Fable or Mythos 5.5 release, or a Fable list price cut
watch.threshold: Reference class: Fable 5.1 came 84 days after Fable 5 and Mythos 5 came 63 days after Mythos Preview. A list price under $10/$50 confirms compression from Opus 5.5. Mythos 5.1 access for UK AISI or non-US organizations would reverse the Sep 24 hold.

watch.item: Next Opus release, its list price and tokenizer
watch.threshold: Reference class: Opus gaps since Nov 2025 ran 42 to 73 days, mean 60, so the window is Nov 3 to Dec 4. List below $4/$20 continues deflation. Flat list with a new tokenizer is an effective rise of up to 35%. No release by Dec 4 breaks the 2026 pattern.

watch.item: Public S-1: Claude Code revenue, price and mix, gross margin definition
watch.threshold: Claude Code above 18% of run-rate or reported as a segment. Adjusted gross margin above 80% reconciled to a GAAP figure. Token or task volumes disclosed. No public S-1 was on EDGAR on Sep 30.

watch.item: US action on Fable 5.1 or Mythos 5.1 access: Commerce letter, UK AISI hold, pre-release review rule
watch.threshold: Reference class: one freeze (Jun 12) and one hold (Sep 24) in 2026. Any disable or hold longer than 24 hours, or a binding pre-release review, turns a one-off into a recurring risk.

watch.item: Retirement notices for Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5
watch.threshold: Earliest retirement dates are Sep 29, Oct 15 and Nov 24 2026, each 12 months after release, with 60 days' notice. Retirement on those dates repeats Opus 4.1's 12-month life. A later date would break the pattern.

watch.item: Ruling on the motion to dismiss in the consolidated Max-plan class action
watch.threshold: Motion filed Sep 22. Denial keeps plan-limit disclosure risk open. Dismissal removes one pressure on flat-plan pricing. No base rate for such rulings is in the record.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the quality claims that would separate fundamentals are vendor-sourced here, with one independent snapshot, so this slice cannot show whether multiples track quality. (b) Confirms the basis rule but cannot test the 39.75% haircut: Anthropic books revenue gross of cloud resale, so list cuts hit reported revenue directly. (e) Confirms: seat and ARR conventions fail when unit price is per token, falling, and moving from seat fees to metered usage. (c) and (d) are not testable from this slice.

The Claude Code figure stops at Feb 2026 and covers the product only, not coding demand arriving through API channels. 2025 gross margin is about 50% (The Information, T3) or 40% (WSJ via a Substack summary, DISPUTED).

The Opus 5.5 '40% less' compares per-task cost with Opus 5, while list price is -20% vs Opus 5 and -60% vs Fable 5.1, and some headlines mix the baselines. Artificial Analysis' blended cost estimate, which depends on token use, has Sonnet 5.5 at $7.60 above Opus 5.5 at $5.98 at max effort, inverting the list ladder.

No industry base rate is in the record. What differs now: the CEO's pacing essay, a voluntary federal pre-release review (single T3 report), RSP revisions and compute limits.

Anthropic names no agency while CSIS names BIS. Restoration is Jul 1 per Anthropic and TechCrunch, and a 'Jun 12 to Jul 7' window elsewhere matches the end of initial plan access. Revenue impact is undisclosed.

topics.title: Moat, competition and market position
topics.one_liner: Most of Anthropic's edge is rented or unproven: two clouds carried 47% of 2025 sales, two customers 12% each, and 63 of 67 logged benchmark entries are vendor-reported.

key_metrics.label: Enterprise and coding share, with basis
key_metrics.value: Menlo, Dec 9 2025 (T3, an Anthropic investor): 54% of enterprise coding, from 42% in Jul, vs OpenAI 21%, a survey of usage; 40% of enterprise LLM API dollars vs OpenAI 27% and Google 21%, estimated dollars, a different basis from Jul's 32% of usage. a16z, Jan 30: OpenAI 78% in production, Anthropic 44%.

key_metrics.label: Customer concentration, FY2025
key_metrics.value: Two unnamed customers at about 12% each, nearly 25% combined, about $1.1B (derived). Most large clients lack long-term contracts. Reuters reading a leaked draft prospectus, Sep 29; no public S-1; names undisclosed.

key_metrics.label: Two-cloud channel share of sales, FY2025
key_metrics.value: 47% ($2.16B) through Amazon and Google marketplaces, from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024. Platforms kept about 16 cents per dollar and collected 60% of year-end receivables. Microsoft Foundry is not broken out.

key_metrics.label: Benchmark position on an independent board
key_metrics.value: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Sep 30 (T3, one undated snapshot): Opus 5.5 58, Sonnet 5.5 56, Fable 5.1 53, GPT-6 Astra 53. 63 of 67 benchmark entries logged in the record are vendor-reported; the 4 independent ones sit in this snapshot.

key_metrics.label: Release cycles per year
key_metrics.value: 13 release dates (15 model rows) in the 12 months to Sep 30 2026, against 5 dates (6 rows) in the prior 12. Median gap between 2026 release dates: 21 days. Desk count from the pricing table.

key_metrics.label: Large-account base
key_metrics.value: 1,000+ customers at $1M or more annualized on Apr 6 2026 (T1), from 500+ on Feb 12 and about a dozen in early 2024; 8 of the Fortune 10 on Feb 12. Retention is estimate-only: PitchBook (T3, LOW) has NRR 140%+, logo churn under 5%.

what.t: Reuters, Sep 29, reading a leaked draft prospectus (single origin, no public S-1): Amazon and Google marketplaces carried 47% of 2025 sales, $2.16B, up from 11% in 2023 and 32% in 2024, and platforms kept about 16 cents per dollar. Two unnamed customers were about 12% each. Most large clients lack long-term contracts. Claude reached Microsoft Foundry in preview Nov 18, 2025 (T1). Not shown: 2026 mix or Azure's share.

Anthropic (T1) counted 1,000+ customers at $1M or more annualized on Apr 6, from 500+ on Feb 12 and about a dozen in early 2024. The last business-customer count, 300,000+, dates from Sep 2025. Retention is estimated only: PitchBook (T3, LOW) has NRR 140%+ and logo churn under 5%. About 10,000 consultants hold Partner Network credentials (Jun 3, T1). Deloitte's 470,000 seats are 'available to'.

Menlo (T3, an Anthropic investor), Dec 9: Anthropic 40% of enterprise API dollars, OpenAI 27%, Google 21%; coding 54% against OpenAI 21%. Claude Code run-rate was over $2.5B on Feb 12 (T1), about 18% of company run-rate, with no later figure; Anthropic cited 4% of public GitHub commits. SpaceX agreed Jun 16 to buy Cursor for $60B (8-K, T1). Not shown: any independent coding revenue share.

Of 67 benchmark entries logged in the record, 63 are vendor-reported. The 4 independent ones come from one undated Sep 30 snapshot (T3). Artificial Analysis scores Opus 5.5 at 58, Sonnet 5.5 at 56, Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra at 53. Arena's agent board has Fable 5.1 first at 14.58% win share, Astra second at 11.78%. Epoch's index, led by Astra at 167, showed no Claude entry.

OpenAI priced GPT-6 Sol at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 on Sep 22, the day Opus 5.5 shipped (SiliconANGLE, T3, single source). Axios (T2) has OpenAI near $70B annualized, basis unstated, against Anthropic's $65B gross at end-July. Google accepted the Pentagon's 'all lawful uses' terms Apr 28 (TechCrunch, T2). Meta was in early lease talks Jul 17, direction unresolved (CNN, T2). Not shown: any Google, Meta or xAI model release.

Anthropic alleged (T1, no lab reply in record) 16M+ distillation exchanges by DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax on Feb 23 and nearly 200M across five campaigns on Sep 10, Alibaba 151M. A June letter said 28.8M for Alibaba (DISPUTED, windows differ). The White House said Jul 22 that Moonshot distilled Fable for Kimi K3 (T2); experts doubted it. CISA, FBI and NSA named six Chinese labs Sep 8, citing Anthropic (T1).

means.t: Channel, supplier, investor and rival are the same few names. Leaked-draft commitments to Amazon, Google and Microsoft are $110B, $111.1B and $31.4B (T3), with about 80% of $518B non-cancelable. SpaceX, which builds Grok and agreed to buy Cursor, sells Colossus on 90 days' notice (T1). Four chip families and a custom-chip hiring push (Aug 5, T2) hedge supply but do not own it. Not shown: any rival's capacity.

Copied: OpenAI announced MCP support 121 days after launch, Microsoft and GitHub by day 175. I count nine dated parity episodes: Anthropic matched four, rivals followed two, three were simultaneous. No Anthropic price cut is tied to a rival move. Held: cloud partners kept Claude available after the Pentagon designation (Mar 6, T2). Anthropic cut off Windsurf and OpenAI, bought Bun and Stainless, and opened MCP and Skills.

Trust pays with regulated buyers and costs with government. Banks co-designed Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (Sep 1, T1), and Claude hit No. 1 on the US App Store Feb 28 (T2). The Pentagon says about 90% of workloads moved (T2), the D.C. Circuit upheld the exclusion 2-1 Sep 25 (T1), and Anthropic's Sep 9 assessment admits harmful actions on real systems. Two March leaks and an April postmortem add operational doubt.

Pricing power shows in terms, not list prices. Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 claims Fable 5.1 performance at a list price 60% lower, 21 days after Fable 5.1 shipped at $10/$50, a tier Washington froze and held. Anthropic added weekly limits, moved Enterprise to $20 seats plus API-rate usage and put Fable on usage credits. Talent flows both ways: Karpathy joined May 19 (T2) and two researchers quit publicly.

implications.t: Durable so far, pending the S-1: the large-enterprise base and regulated-industry trust. Customers at $1M+ rose from 500+ to 1,000+ across the Pentagon designation. The only recorded losses are federal: three contractors terminated and three deals over $180M fell apart (sworn declarations, T1). It drops to unproven if the S-1 shows NRR under 100%, a 12% customer leaving, or fewer than 1,000 at $1M+. Give moat credit here first.

Rented: distribution, compute and coding channels. Two clouds carried 47% of sales, Amazon and Google are owed $110B and $111.1B of a $518B plan (T3), and SpaceX, buying Cursor, sells compute on 90 days' notice. It improves if the S-1 shows channel share at or below 47% with Foundry broken out, or more 20-year leases like TeraWulf's. Do not treat partner growth as a moat.

Unproven: model-quality lead, the release cadence behind it, switching costs, pricing power, talent and distillation defense. The lead rests on one independent snapshot. Promote the lead if two updates keep Claude 5 points ahead on Artificial Analysis; demote it if the gap falls to 2 or Astra tops Claude on Arena at matched effort. Show vendor and independent benchmarks on separate axes.

second_order: Research is published, so talent is the moat question. Anthropic released its Constitution under CC0 (Jan 22) and circuit-tracing tools (May 29, 2025), so methods can be copied, and people move both ways: Karpathy joined May 19, researchers quit Feb 9 and Sep 8. Anthropic says Claude writes over 80% of its merged code. If that speeds research, velocity compounds. With no attrition series, consensus credits research leadership without a retention measure.

Distillation can make the lead a wasting asset. Disclosed exchanges rose from 16M+ on Feb 23 to nearly 200M on Sep 10. On Jul 22, 21 days after Fable's return, the White House said Moonshot distilled it for Kimi K3 and Treasury said sanctions were possible; experts doubted the claim. The draft prospectus, paraphrased, ties demand to continuous releases, so the 21-day median release gap may be the cost of staying ahead.

Intermediaries route on price and quality each release. Named partners that disclose other vendors carry rivals: Copilot (Gemini, o1), Harvey (OpenAI, Gemini), Xcode 26.3 (Codex), Alexa+ (Nova), DuckDuckGo (OpenAI). Menlo's mid-2025 survey had 11% of respondents switching vendors (T3), and TechCrunch's Ramp read says businesses flip between labs as models launch. Until retention is disclosed, the $1M customer count does not show lock-in.

Cursor is the first case of a rival owning a top coding channel. SpaceX collects $1.25B a month from Anthropic for Colossus (T1), builds Grok and agreed to buy Cursor, closing reported Aug 15, unverified. One employee put Cursor at 40% to 50% of Anthropic revenue early on (T3, LOW). If Claude stays Cursor's default two quarters after closing, coding share was earned. If not, it was rented.

Open-weight pressure shows in tokens, not enterprise dollars. Open models held 13% of enterprise workloads in Jul 2025 (Menlo, T3) and 6.4% of AI spenders in Sep (Ramp via FourWeekMBA, T4), yet Chinese models carried over 45% of OpenRouter traffic and Claude's token share fell to 13.3% from 29.1% (T4). If tokens lead dollars, deflation reaches enterprise next. Consensus may read dollar share as the whole market.

watch.item: Ramp AI Index October edition and any Menlo enterprise update (none since Dec 9, 2025)
watch.threshold: The Sep read is T4: 43.8% vs 39.8%, a 4.0-point gap. Compare only within one Ramp release, since May was restated from 34.4% to 41%. OpenAI closing the gap two editions running, or Menlo dollar share under 40%, points to flipping, not lock-in.

watch.item: Independent benchmark updates for Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 on Artificial Analysis, Arena and Epoch, plus OpenRouter's top-10 slots (5 of 10 on Sep 29, T3)
watch.threshold: Reference class: one snapshot, so no base rate. Opus 5.5 at 58 against Astra at 53 is the base. A lead of 2 points or less, Astra above Claude on Arena at matched effort, or fewer than 5 Claude slots demotes quality. A 5-point lead held over two updates, or a Claude entry on Epoch, promotes it.

watch.item: Claude inside Cursor after SpaceX's $60B purchase: default model, availability, and Cursor's share of AI-coding spend on Ramp (41% Jun 2025, about 26% May 2026, T3 LOW)
watch.threshold: Reference class: Anthropic cut off Windsurf on under five days' notice (Jun 2025) and OpenAI (Aug 2025); the record has no case of a rival-owned channel. Claude removed or demoted as default means coding share was rented. Claude kept as default for two quarters after close supports earned share.

watch.item: Public S-1 customer note: the two 12% customers, H1 2026 concentration, contract terms, net expansion, count of customers at $1M+
watch.threshold: Any customer above 10% in H1 2026 means concentration persisted. NRR under 120%, PitchBook's own risk flag, or fewer than 1,000 customers at $1M+ demotes the enterprise base. Multiyear contracts covering most large clients would contradict Reuters.

watch.item: Public S-1 channel data for H1 2026: marketplace share, fee rate, Microsoft Foundry broken out
watch.threshold: Above 47% or a fee above 16 cents moves distribution further into rented. At or below 47% with direct revenue growing faster would reverse the 11%, 32%, 47% trend.

watch.item: Rival price moves after Anthropic releases: OpenAI, Google or xAI list prices against Sonnet 5.5 at $2/$10 and Opus 5.5 at $4/$20, and Haiku 5.5 against Luna at $0.10/$0.50
watch.threshold: The only dated pair is Sep 22, same day, T3, single source. A second rival cut within a week of an Anthropic release shows a matching pattern. A rival flagship at or below $4/$20 with comparable independent scores ends Anthropic's price parity.

watch.item: Q3 2026 results shown to investors before the November listing (WSJ, T3): Claude Code run-rate, customers at $1M+, largest customers
watch.threshold: Claude Code was over $2.5B, 18% of run-rate, on Feb 12. A higher share means coding is gaining; a lower share means it was diluted. Customers at $1M+ were 1,000+ on Apr 6.

watch.item: Senior research departures or hires: a third public resignation after Feb 9 and Sep 8, or a named hire from OpenAI, Google DeepMind or Meta
watch.threshold: Two public resignations in eight months is the record's only base rate; no attrition series exists. A third inside one quarter of listing tests the talent claim. A marquee hire after the listing supports it.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: equal multiples can hide unequal durability, since two clouds carried 47% of sales and 63 of 67 benchmark entries are vendor-reported, though this slice holds no rival durability data. (b) Not supported: the partner fee is about 7.6% of FY2025 revenue (Reuters, T3), far below a 39.75% haircut, and this slice has no derivation of that figure. (c) Not tested here. (d) Not tested here. (e) Confirms: SaaS retention conventions fail, since Deloitte's 470,000 seats are 'available to', Enterprise is $20 per seat plus API-rate usage, and no NRR is disclosed.

uncertainties.note: Share series are not like-for-like and two are investor or derivative. Menlo is an Anthropic investor and moved from usage to estimated dollars between Jul and Dec 2025. a16z has OpenAI 78% to Anthropic 44% in production. Ramp's May read is 34.4% vs 32.3% in the release and 41% vs 39% restated, and its Sep read is T4. OpenRouter is T4. No independent revenue share exists.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: A primary Ramp table, an independent spend survey, or the S-1 revenue split by product and channel.

uncertainties.note: Retention and contract terms are estimates or single-source. NRR 140%+, churn under 5% and over 50% multiyear are PitchBook estimates (T3, LOW). Reuters says most large clients lack long-term contracts, and the two populations are not reconcilable on this record. The two 12% customers are unnamed, and the record does not say whether either is a coding channel. FY2025 shares may not describe a run-rate that grew from about $9B to over $65B gross.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 customer note, contract-term disclosure and any net expansion rate.

uncertainties.note: Model-quality evidence is one undated T3 snapshot. Boards use different effort settings, Opus 5.5 at max on one and High on another. OpenRouter's index values sit within 0.4 of Artificial Analysis, so they are probably not a second check (my inference). Epoch showed no Claude entries. The record has no Gemini, Llama or Grok releases, so rivals are unmeasured.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Dated independent histories at matched effort, replication of the Terminal-Bench 4.0 claims, and rival releases entered in the record.

uncertainties.note: The durable, rented and unproven ranking is my judgment. Contract terms that decide 'rented' are not public, and the record shows no revenue lost to the Jun 12 freeze, no attrition series and no cost per token. Thresholds such as a 5-point Artificial Analysis lead are desk choices, since the index's normal movement is not in the record.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: S-1 commitments and related-party notes, cloud contract terms, and several independent benchmark updates that show index volatility.

uncertainties.note: Persistence of any advantage is a forecast. Reference class in the record: nine dated parity episodes, with rival matches arriving from the same week to 175 days. No industry base rate for moat decay in AI models is in the record. What differs here: a 21-day median release gap in 2026, about 80% non-cancelable compute, and outputs that are distilled.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Two independent benchmark updates after a rival release, or a disclosed loss of a top customer or channel.

topics.title: Governance, control structure and safety policy
topics.one_liner: Leaked draft prospectus, Sep 28: one Class F share gives seven founders 50.1% of votes and the Trust elects 4 of 7 directors. No public S-1 exists.

key_metrics.label: Founder vote share (Class F)
key_metrics.value: 50.1% of total voting power on key matters, held by one Class F share that seven co-founders direct by majority (Reuters, T2). Holds while three keep a minimum stake, amount unreported (The Information, T3). About 2% economic stake each (T3).

key_metrics.label: LTBT board-seat share
key_metrics.value: 4 of 7 seats (57%) elected by the Trust after IPO (Reuters, T2). Three of six named directors look Trust-linked today on the record's arithmetic (Hastings, Narasimhan, Liddell), so the fourth seat is open or unnamed. The T1 majority of Apr 14 reportedly lasted about five weeks (Kreps exit, T5).

key_metrics.label: Board size
key_metrics.value: 6 directors named in the draft prospectus: Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei (chair), Razavi, Hastings, Liddell, Narasimhan. 7 seats after IPO: 4 Trust, 3 Class F and Class A. Anthropic stated 6 members on Feb 13; its Apr 14 post implies 7.

key_metrics.label: Lock-up status
key_metrics.value: Unreported. No lock-up length in any opened prospectus coverage. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; T4 relays) says lock-ups beyond the standard 180 days are weighed, with insider sales in the offering and preset 10b5-1 plans for staff.

key_metrics.label: Trustees in office
key_metrics.value: 3 (Shah chair, Fontaine, Bernanke) versus 5 founding trustees on Sep 19, 2023. Four of five founders left by Jan 2026. Cuéllar left Aug 4, about 6.5 months after joining, to become Chief Global Affairs Officer.

key_metrics.label: RSP revision cadence
key_metrics.value: 9 versions since Sep 19, 2023. Five in 2026: v3.0 on Feb 24 to v3.4 on Jul 8, 19 weeks. v3.4 is the latest in the record, 84 days old at Sep 30.

what.t: Anthropic disclosed the Long-Term Benefit Trust on Sep 19, 2023 (T1). It holds Class T stock and was to elect a board majority within four years. Four of the five founding trustees have left: Matheny (Dec 2023), Christiano (Apr 2024), Bahl and Robinson (Jan 2026). Fontaine joined in 2025, Cuéllar in Jan 2026 (left Aug 4) and Bernanke in Jul 2026. Three trustees remain.

Trust-appointed directors arrived one at a time: Kreps May 29, 2024, Hastings May 28, 2025, Narasimhan Apr 14, 2026. Anthropic then said they were a board majority (T1). Kreps reportedly left about May 22 (T5, community sources). The draft prospectus names six directors: two executive Amodeis, with Daniela as chair, plus Razavi (Spark Capital), Hastings, Liddell, Narasimhan. Liddell's appointer and director independence are unstated.

Reuters' review of the draft prospectus (Sep 28, T2): a Founder LLC of seven co-founders directs one Class F share carrying 50.1% of votes on key matters. Class A gets one vote per share. The Trust elects four of seven directors. Other classes give strategic partners minimal votes and, per The Information (T3), employees tie-break stock. Amazon's notes convert to nonvoting common at IPO, subject to a cap (10-Q, T1).

RSP v1.0 (Sep 19, 2023) set ASL levels; changes needed board approval after Trust consultation. v2.0 (Oct 15, 2024) added capability thresholds. ASL-3 first applied to Opus 4 on May 22, 2025. v3.0 (Feb 24, 2026) added non-binding roadmap targets and Risk Reports. v3.2 gave the Trust review powers. v3.4 (Jul 8) cut unredacted Risk Report sharing from all cleared staff to at least 200 employees.

No public S-1 exists on EDGAR (Sep 30). Reuters' review of the leaked draft (T2) confirms existential risk, shutdown resistance, concealment, blackmail-like behavior, evaluation awareness, unsettled agent liability and governance that may conflict with financial interests. About 6% of research compute went to safety in a July week (T3). No coverage, inference only: Pentagon, export controls, RSP changes, key-person risk. About 80 of 261 pages are risk factors.

No opened prospectus coverage states a lock-up. The Information (Aug 27, Sep 3; T4 relays of a T3 scoop) says lock-ups beyond 180 days are weighed, insiders may sell in the offering and staff may face preset 10b5-1 plans. The Sep 3 relay is tagged DISPUTED on raise size. Earlier: a May 2025 buyback at $61.5B (T3) and a Feb 2026 tender planned at $350B pre-money (T3, completion unconfirmed).

means.t: Three instruments split control. The PBC charter lets directors weigh public benefit against financial interest, yet no decision or suit in the record cites it. Class T gives a no-equity Trust four seats. Class F gives seven founders, about 2% each (T3), half the vote by majority rule. Amazon and Google hold large stakes with no or minimal votes. Class A holders vote but cannot outvote Class F (inference).

The Trust's edge is seat math. Pre-IPO text (T1): trustees pick successors with Anthropic's input and hold no equity, and a stockholder supermajority can amend the Trust without trustee consent. Post-IPO thresholds are not public. If measured on total votes, Class F can block any supermajority change (inference). Since Apr 2024 no trustee is described as an AI researcher, yet RSP v3.2 gave the Trust Risk Report review rights.

The RSP binds only by Anthropic's choice, and Anthropic rewrites it often. Three of five 2026 revisions edited a threshold: v3.1 (Apr 2), v3.3 (May 26), v3.4 (Jul 8). implications.t: Reprice control, not mission. Treat Class A as a claim on economics with no route to a vote the founders oppose. Carry the Trust as a thin, self-perpetuating check until the public S-1 shows Class T amendment thresholds, the minimum-stake amount, sunset terms and the fourth Trust seat. Until then do not credit governance as a moat.

Score the RSP as disclosure plus outside review, not a covenant. Track Risk Reports, Trust-requested external reviews and the METR investigation, not ASL labels. Per v3.1 a pause is Anthropic's choice, not an RSP trigger (inference). About 80% of the $518B compute plan is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2), so the pause option has a price.

Treat governance as event risk, neither a proven moat nor a booked liability. Realized federal loss is small against run-rate: PitchBook puts the ban near $200M, about 1.4% of ARR (T3), while sworn filings claim far more at risk, unrealized. Reprice on a second suspension, a FASCSA escalation or issued FTC demands.

Show every governance figure with its tier. Structure is leak-based (Reuters, T2) until EDGAR carries it. Show the Kreps exit (T5), about 2% per founder (T3) and lock-up ideas (T4) as unconfirmed, and gate the control metrics on the public S-1.

second_order: A single Class F share at 50.1% makes Class A votes irrelevant to any outcome the founders oppose (inference), and Amazon and Google hold no or minimal votes. The live contest is founders versus Trust, not founders versus investors. Index committees and proxy advisers must rule on a powerless float. If the Nasdaq-100 fast-entry rule applies, 15 trading days after listing (Motley Fool, T4), passive funds would be buying within weeks.

The Trust gained RSP review powers on Apr 29, two weeks after its board majority, then lost the majority (reportedly May 22) and a trustee (Aug 4). Mandate rose as the bench thinned. If the Trust does not refill seats before a roadshow, the S-1 will describe three trustees and six sitting directors. This falsifies a reading of the four-year plan as a steady ramp in outside control.

Take-or-pay commitments make a pause expensive. About 80% of the $518B compute plan is non-cancelable or payable regardless of use (T2). Yet the draft reportedly says slowing the technology 'would likely be a good thing' (T3), and Anthropic backs a pause option (Jun 4) and slowing (Sep 12). Critics call that positioning or capture (Sacks, T3). The commitments show a cost, and Class A holders would bear it without a deciding vote (inference).

Anthropic's June framework asked for legal authority to block dangerous deployments (dated Jun 1 in one record event, Jun 10 in another). A US export-control directive then cut two models on Jun 12, and Anthropic's reply asked for a statutory, transparent process (T1). On Anthropic's own account the dispute is process, not power. The White House hold on Mythos 5.1 (Sep 24) and the FTC probe (Sep 30) extend executive discretion that no Anthropic governance body can veto.

Liquidity design looks like supply management (inference). Insider sales in the offering would meet demand at launch, while a lock-up beyond 180 days with a second window and preset 10b5-1 plans (T4 relays) would hold the rest back. A reported Nvidia anchor of up to $10B is about 0.5% at $2T (T3). Amazon's nonvoting block, capped at an undisclosed level, sets the overhang. This bears on the absorption thesis.

what.t: Bartz v. Anthropic: a court order (T1) gave final approval on Jul 20, 2026 to a non-reversionary $1.5B class settlement over 482,460 works, about $3,109 each (derived), with $101.56M in fees and dismissal with prejudice. The Jun 23, 2025 ruling held training fair use but the pirated library not. A T3 schedule puts $450M due Sep 25, 2027.

Suits followed the signing: Carreyrou opt-outs (Dec 22, 2025, T2), Concord II (Jan 28, 20,517 works, Amodei and Mann named), BMG (Mar 17, T2), Cognella and Chicken Soup (May), Round Hill (Aug 17), Sony and Warner Chappell (Aug 28). Concord I fair-use summary judgment is heard Oct 21. Reddit survived a demurrer on 3 of 5 claims Sep 17 (T3).

Pentagon: a Jan 9 memo demanded 'any lawful use'. Feb 27 directives and a Mar 3 FASCSA determination followed. N.D. Cal. enjoined Mar 26 and on Aug 27 vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and contractor boycott (orders, T1). The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion 2-1 on Sep 25, Henderson dissenting, mandate withheld (opinion, T1). Michael says Anthropic is still designated (Sep 3, T3).

A Commerce directive at 5:21pm ET on Jun 12 barred foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Anthropic disabled both worldwide (Anthropic, T1; BIS per CSIS, T2). Mythos 5 was partly approved Jun 26, controls lifted Jun 30, Fable 5 restored Jul 1. On Sep 24 the National Cyber Director's office asked Anthropic to hold Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI; it complied (Politico, T2).

Anthropic's Nov 13, 2025 report said a Chinese state-sponsored group ran 80-90% of an espionage campaign on about 30 targets via Claude Code (company claim, T1). Its Sep 10 report adds Russian and Chinese espionage and about 200M distillation exchanges, Alibaba 151M on 3,500 accounts. The June letter said Alibaba 28.8M on about 25,000 accounts (DISPUTED). CISA, FBI and NSA named six Chinese firms Sep 8 (T1).

Anthropic disclosed three incidents on Jul 30 and a fourth, from January, on Sep 9 (T1) in which Claude models accessed real systems; Mythos 5's malicious PyPI package ran on 15 systems. The FTC opened a probe of Anthropic, OpenAI and METR on agentic AI on Sep 30, citing the Jul 30 breaches (Reuters via Yahoo, T2, single source, first reported by the New York Post).

means.t: Bartz held training on lawfully acquired books fair use and piracy not. Exposure turns on how data was obtained, priced per work up to $150,000. The $1.5B releases past conduct on listed works and is no licence for future training. It is one-time for that class but recurs class by class, since most new complaints plead the same piracy theory. Reddit's contract claims sit outside fair use.

Two instruments produced two outcomes. N.D. Cal. vacated the 10 U.S.C. 3252 designation and the contractor boycott on First Amendment, due-process and APA grounds. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion, finding Anthropic's refusal of 'all lawful uses', not its speech, caused it. Defense and Defense Industrial Base use stays excluded. Civil-agency eligibility is restored unless the government wins on appeal.

The June directive was a letter with no specifics or process. Nationality could not be verified in real time, so Anthropic shut both models for all users. Restoration required cyber classifiers with an Opus 4.8 fallback, pre-release government access and malicious-activity reporting. Both Mythos-class launches (Jun 9, Sep 1) drew federal action, the Jun 12 recall and the Sep 24 hold. Four other launches drew none in the record.

Dollar exposure exists only where a per-unit formula does. Copyright has one, statutory damages per work, so 2 of 39 rows carry a liability figure: Bartz $1.5B and Concord II's theoretical $3B. Government actions have no price, and the Pentagon's only figure is Anthropic's own declaration. Pentagon, export, FTC and security matters hit access and revenue, so they show up as lost customers, delays and disclosure.

implications.t: Model the $1.5B as a one-time charge for listed works and copyright as serial claims. Reference class: Bartz, the only settlement in the record, at $3,109 per work, 2.1% of the statutory maximum (derived). On 35,874 counted music works that is about $112M, against $5.4B at the ceiling (derived). Sony and Warner Chappell counts are not in the record. Re-mark after Oct 21.

Treat Pentagon workload revenue as largely lost and commercial spillover as contingent. The March declaration sized 2026 revenue risk at hundreds of millions to multiple billions when run-rate was $14B (T1, gross) to $19B (T3). Run-rate is $65B now (T2, gross), and Judge Lin vacated the contractor boycott. The Pentagon says about 90% of workloads moved, though NSA use of Mythos is reported (T3).

Top two by dollars: music suits (ceiling $5.4B) and the Pentagon declaration (multiple billions, uncapped). Then Bartz cash due ($450M) and opt-outs (ceiling $270M). Bartz, music and opt-out figures sum to about $7.2B, 0.74% of the $965B mark (ceilings and sums derived). By timing: FTC probe, D.C. Circuit review, Oct 21 hearing, METR report. The S-1 is not yet public (T1); check it covers all four.

Likely risk-factor topics, by cases-table notes: Bartz, music, publisher and opt-out suits, Reddit, the Pentagon label, the June recall, the FTC probe, eval incidents, distillation. Among these, press confirms only self-preservation, agentic legal risk and (T4, VERIFY) backlash language. Treat recall and hold power as an operating risk. Check the S-1 for Commerce's reported right to reimpose restrictions (T4) and SB 53 incident reporting.

second_order: Valuation is now a litigation input. Concord II pleaded a $350B+ valuation and Sony and Warner Chappell pleaded $965B, arguing $1.5B does not deter. A listing near $2T (WSJ, T3) hands the next plaintiff a larger anchor, so per-work asks may track market cap. Underwriters, insurers and counsel must price that. Consensus may treat Bartz as a ceiling; plaintiffs cite it as a floor.

The Pentagon dispute may end by politics, not judgment. The rulings rest on different statutes and courts, and Anthropic is considering further review with no deadline in the record. Meanwhile Lutnick signals the security rift is over (Sep 2, T3), Trump and Amodei dined Sep 27 (date inferred), and Amodei signed the Sep 29 voluntary pact. Consensus watches the courts; the lever may be the White House.

Regulators converge on one capability. Commerce (recall), the National Cyber Director (hold), the FTC (developer liability, single source), the Pentagon (exclusion), the EU (watermarking from Aug 2) and California (SB 53 incident reports) all act on cyber-capable agents. OpenAI is named beside Anthropic in the FTC probe and the hold, so the burden is sector-wide: a timing risk for a crowded IPO window, not a relative discount.

Security events now cross into legal and policy. UTRF's Jul 20 patent complaint cites internal Claude Code file names such as autoDream.ts, which the record infers came from the Mar 31 leak. Distillation claims drive policy asks, yet Alibaba account counts differ about 7x (derived) between the June letter and the September report, over different windows. Challenged counts would weaken the tailwind.

Advocacy has become a liability. Amodei's Sep 12 pacing essay is cited in the Buist antitrust complaint (Sep 18), Sacks called the push regulatory capture (Sep 13, T3), and WSJ (T3) ties the November slip to scrutiny after the CEO's pace warnings. A safety-first stance now carries antitrust and timing cost. Consensus may treat the policy stance as brand; the record shows legal and IPO consequences.

Circuit denied Anthropic's petitions 2-1 on Sep 25 and upheld the FASCSA exclusion (T1). Under Secretary Michael said Sep 11 that about 90% of workloads had moved (DefenseScoop, T2, single source).
