Policy line. Qualified support for SB 1047 on Aug 21, 2024 (T3) ended in a veto Sep 29. Anthropic endorsed SB 53 Sep 8, 2025 (T1), in force Jan 1, 2026. It gave $20M to Public First Action Feb 12. A June 2026 framework seeks federal power to block dangerous deployments. The Sep 12 'pace the frontier' essay sought an antitrust waiver; Sacks called it capture Sep 13 (T3).

International. Offices opened: London May 2023 (VERIFY), Zurich Feb 2025, Tokyo Oct 29, 2025, Bengaluru Feb 16, Sydney Apr 27, Milan May 27 and Seoul Jun 17, 2026. Dublin, Paris and Munich lack opening dates. Sovereign MoUs: UK Feb 2025, Japan Oct 2025, Rwanda Feb 2026, Australia Mar 2026 and Korea Jun 2026 (all T1).

means.t: Exposure is federal discretion, not contract revenue. On my arithmetic the CDAO ceiling is at most 0.7% of the $14B run-rate on Feb 12, and pre-ban public-sector ARR above $500M (Reuters, T2) is over 3.6%. In seven months the government pulled five levers: agency ban, contractor boycott, model suspension, foreign-access hold and an FTC probe. The Jun 12 letter gave no specifics.

Strategy: back binding rules that bind every large lab, preferably federal, with state laws as an interim step. SB 53 covers 10^26 FLOPs and firms above $500M revenue. The June framework covers 10^25 FLOPs and $500M AI revenue or $1B R&D, with penalties tied to global revenue. Abroad the record shows codes and MoUs: EU code signatory, watermarking after Aug 2, institute MoUs, no UK or Asian statute.

Evidence policy helps. Anthropic published an SB 53 compliance framework before the law took effect. Its Feb 23 distillation post was cited by the Sep 8 CISA, FBI and NSA advisory on six Chinese labs. Treasury urged banks to test Mythos (T3), Commerce approved it for 100+ US institutions (T2), and NSA reportedly uses it (T3). Claude hit No. 1 on the App Store Feb 28 (T2).

Evidence policy hurts. DoD moved workloads to OpenAI, Google and xAI, and Google agreed to 'all lawful uses' Apr 28 (T2). Two models went dark 18 days on a directive that gave no specifics. FTC footnotes cite Anthropic over six times and xAI once (Tech Times, T3). Pacing advocacy drew a Sherman Act suit Sep 18. The PRC ban forwent several hundred million dollars, per Amodei.

implications.t: My read (interpretation): policy is neither a moat nor a revenue liability yet. It is event risk. Realized loss is $150M of DoD ARR (Reuters, T2) plus delayed contractor deals, while run-rate still rose $14B to $65B (gross, not recognized revenue, no counterfactual). Reprice tails: another suspension, FTC findings, FASCSA spillover. Rules exempt small labs and, on their thresholds, bind rivals equally, so the edge is enforcement discretion.

Legal map. The 3252 and FASCSA tracks point opposite ways, so the S-1 should describe two instruments. The D.C. Circuit result controls DoW and contractor use. Track the mandate, en banc or cert, the stayed Ninth Circuit appeal and any government appeal of the Aug 27 judgment. Treat the Sep 2 to Sep 29 thaw as White House and Commerce, not DoW.

International: treat MoUs as options, not revenue; only Australia names dollars (A$3M in credits). Anthropic says APAC run-rate rose over 10x and EMEA over 9x, with no dollars. India is second by volume at 5.8% of Claude.ai use but 101st per working-age capita. Volta, Norway, is the only named non-US compute site (T2). Singapore is due in October (Fortune, T2); announce-to-open lags run 33 to 237 days.

Regulation: score the 'regulatory capture' charge as political risk, not proof of a moat. Watch the House preemption draft and the November midterms, where Anthropic's $20M and AnthroPAC meet an OpenAI-linked network above $100M. Anthropic's position on the draft is not in the record. Ask for it before pricing the durability of SB 53 and similar state laws.

second_order: The Pentagon exit moves classified reference workloads, including Palantir Maven, to OpenAI, Google and xAI. OpenAI's Feb 27 terms named prohibitions close to Anthropic's two exceptions, so the fight reads as control over who enforces limits, not the limits. Contractors must certify non-use. Coverage frames the Sep 27 dinner as a thaw. DoW says the designation stands.

The Jun 12 and Sep 24 actions make foreign access to frontier models a US executive decision. UK AISI, Anthropic's deepest government partner abroad, is the first ally held back by name. Japan, Australia and Korea MoUs cover safety evaluation and model information that the same gate can block. This tests whether sovereign MoUs are a durable channel: the record shows no MoU dollars and two US gates.

Pacing advocacy opened a legal channel. The Buist complaint cites Amodei's Sep 12 essay as evidence of agreement, and the desk's case note expects discovery into any industry working group. Altman endorsed the essay and Musk said Dario is right, and their companies are co-defendants. The public debate is about motive. The docket is about conduct.

The moat case weakens as rivals converge. OpenAI's Chris Lehane opposed SB 53 and an OpenAI-linked PAC network has over $100M, yet by Sep 2026 OpenAI shared the pacing endorsement, the UN briefing, the White House hold and the FTC probe. When rules bind every large lab, the differentiator is how much discretion the executive applies to each.

Washington access did not insulate. A NAIAC seat (2022), a bipartisan advisory council (Aug 2025), a DC office (Mar 2026) and a PAC (Apr 2026) sit on either side of the Feb 27 ban. The thaw ran through Wiles, Bessent, Lutnick and Trump. New government-affairs hires on Aug 4 and Sep 7 add access; the record shows discretion outweighing it.

topics.one_liner: No recorded C-suite exits in 12 months, yet control is redrawn: seven co-founders would get 50.1% of votes on ~2% stakes; the Trust elects 4 of 7 seats.

what.t: Headcount points are few and partly disputed. About 40 staff at the Apr 29, 2022 Series B (T1). Late 2023 reads under 200 or about 500 in two Fortune pieces two days apart, and about 300 per Crunchbase (T3). About 2,300 in Dec 2025 (Fortune, T2), about 2,500 on Jan 30, 2026 (SFist, T3). March 2026 aggregator estimates split at about 3,000 and about 5,000 (T4).

Rahul Patil joined as CTO (Oct 7, 2025, T1; TechCrunch Oct 2) and Sam McCandlish became Chief Architect. On Jan 13, 2026 Mike Krieger moved from CPO to co-lead Labs and Ami Vora took Product (T1). Tino Cuéllar became first Chief Global Affairs Officer on Aug 4 (T1). Reuters' Sep 28 factbox lists eight executives: four founders, four hired since May 2024. The record shows no C-suite exits.

Six directors by appointer: founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, investors' seat Yasmin Razavi, Trust Reed Hastings (May 28, 2025) and Vas Narasimhan (Apr 14, 2026), unstated Chris Liddell (Feb 13, 2026). The board grew from four in May 2024 to seven on Apr 14, 2026, a Trust majority (T1). Trust-appointed Jay Kreps reportedly left May 22 (T5, T4 only). Trustees fell to three when Cuéllar left Aug 4.

Reuters (Sep 28, T2) reviewed a leaked draft prospectus. A Founder LLC of seven co-founders directs one Class F share with 50.1% of votes on key matters. The Trust elects four directors; Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and one other are elected by Class F and Class A holders. The Information, via TechCrunch (Sep 25), adds about 2% each and a three-of-seven minimum-stake test. EDGAR shows no public S-1.

Inbound: Jan Leike (May 2024), John Schulman (Aug 2024), Durk Kingma (Oct 2024), Neil Houlsby from DeepMind (Feb 2025), Andrej Karpathy (May 19, 2026), Dale Finlay from OpenAI (Sep 16, 2026). Schulman left after five months for Mira Murati's startup (T2 relay). Mrinank Sharma (Feb 9, T3) and Jacob Coxon (Sep 8, T2) resigned publicly. Jenny Wen to Cursor rests on a T4 tracker.

Buyback on May 2, 2025: up to 20% of employee shares, $2M per person, two-year tenure, $56.09 a share at $61.5B (T3, single outlet). Tender planned Feb 4, 2026 at $350B pre-money (Bloomberg via aggregator, T3). May 12: Anthropic voided transfers on named secondary platforms (T2). Aug 27: staff may sell inside the IPO and lock-ups may run long (The Information, T4, VERIFY).

means.t: Revenue per head rose because run-rate outran hiring. Run-rate went from about $100M in Sep 2023 (T3, basis unstated) to about $9B at end-2025 (company, gross, T1), roughly 90x, while staff grew 4.6x to at least 11.5x on the disputed base. That is $0.2M-$0.5M per head in late 2023 and $3.9M at end-2025. Recognized FY2025 is $2.0M per head, as recognized revenue trails run-rate in a fast-growing year.

Control sits in two hands. After the IPO the Trust elects 4 of 7 seats. Founders hold 50.1% of votes through Class F, so on this reading they decide the other 3 seats and Class A holders cannot outvote them. Sitting trustees pick new ones with Anthropic, hold no equity, and four of five founding trustees left within 28 months. Post-IPO Class T amendment thresholds are not public.

IPO-readiness hires came in a dated run: CFO Krishna Rao (May 21, 2024), Wilson Sonsini (FT, Dec 2, 2025), ex-Microsoft CFO Chris Liddell to the board (Feb 13, 2026), Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan (Apr 14), confidential S-1 (Jun 1), Cuéllar (Aug 4), legal reshuffle (Aug 26, T4), Matt Clifford (Sep 7, T3). The record ties the policy hires to the Pentagon dispute, so the IPO signal is mixed.

Equity is both the retention lever and the exit risk. Series H ($965B post-money) is 15.7x the May 2025 buyback valuation and 2.6x the tender's pre-money ($900B against $350B). Stock also buys teams: Coefficient Bio, about 10 staff for a reported $400M all-stock, and Runhouse, share-based. The two recorded public resignations cite values, not pay.

implications.t: Hold revenue per head as provisional until the S-1 states headcount. Use $3.9M at end-2025 and $5.6M at Feb 2026, both gross run-rate. The 2,500 versus 5,000 split halves any 2026 figure: annualized Q2 recognized revenue of $46B is $18.4M per head at 2,500 and $9.2M at 5,000. The record has no Q2 headcount.

Treat control as two keys and flag it in both cases. The Trust holds a seat majority by design but has three trustees and, on the best reading, three seated directors today. Founders hold the votes, and the draft warns this could conflict with Class A holders' interests. Price no governance discount until the S-1 shows Class T amendment thresholds, the Class F minimum stake and any sunset.

Rank key-person risk with Daniela Amodei first: Dario Amodei says his only direct report is his chief of staff and all other executives report to her (T3), and she chairs the board. Then Dario Amodei as policy voice, Jared Kaplan (CSO and Responsible Scaling Officer since Oct 2024), Jack Clark (Institute, Mar 11, 2026), Krishna Rao (runs the IPO) and Rahul Patil. Co-founder retention is seven of seven.

Carry employee supply as an unknown, not zero. The record has no lock-up length, no insider-sale size and no stock-compensation figure. Staff may sell inside the offering and lock-ups may exceed the norm (T4, VERIFY). Keep float and overhang as open inputs to the IPO-absorption case until the S-1 states them.

second_order: If the Trust's fourth seat is vacant and Liddell counts as Trust-appointed, the Trust elects three of six today, not a majority. The S-1 board section must show the count. What is easy to miss: the record shows three self-selected trustees, one of whom became an executive, and no Anthropic statement of the split after Apr 14.

Two public resignations on safety grounds (Feb 9, Sep 8), the second 20 days before the leaked prospectus, bracket RSP v3.4 (Jul 8), which cut mandatory sharing of unredacted Risk Reports to at least 200 employees. The record shows no link. S-1 drafters must word key-personnel and dissent risk with care. Liquidity alone will not hold staff whose stated reason is values.

Staff who sold in the tender at $350B pre-money sold at about 39% of the May Series H pre-money, and the IPO is reported at $2T or more. Lock-up expiry, not the IPO, becomes the retention test. Anthropic must carry staff past that date; the record holds no vesting or refresh-grant data and names no outbound move to OpenAI.

Fortune's seven co-founders omit Ben Mann, whom Anthropic's Labs post calls a co-founder, and prospectus coverage does not list the seven. If Mann sits outside the Founder LLC, a Labs co-lead is outside the control bloc. The S-1's named Founder LLC members settle it.

Two UK appointments, Rishi Sunak (Oct 9, 2025) and Matt Clifford (Sep 7, 2026), drew conflict-of-interest questions, and Clifford stays ARIA chair until Nov 6. The D.C. Circuit upheld the FASCSA exclusion on Sep 25. A policy arm staffed between Aug 4 and Sep 7 may face related-party and adviser disclosure in the S-1.

They kept about 16 cents a dollar and collected 60% of receivables. Two unnamed customers were 12% each (T2). Snowflake committed $200M (Dec 3, T1). Deloitte's 470,000 seats are 'available to'. Bedrock reports over 100,000 customers (Apr 20, T1).

Closed deals are small. Coefficient Bio ~$400M in stock (Apr 3, T2) and Stainless above $300M (May 18) are single-source; Bun, Vercept, Humanloop and Runhouse are unpriced. Decart (~$6B) and MatX (~$7B) talks lapsed (Sep 8, Aug 27). The $100M Anthology Fund (Jul 17 2024) is Menlo's money. Of PitchBook's 35 investments only Goodfire and Sapiom are direct; Basecamp, Sazabi, Frontier and Theseus are not shown as equity.

Menlo (Dec 9 2025, T3) has Anthropic at 40% of API dollars to OpenAI's 27%. a16z (Jan 30, T3) has OpenAI at 78% in production to Anthropic's 44%. Ramp card data (Aug 20, T3) has 44% to 40% in July, from 41% to 39% in May. Axios (Sep 29, T2, single source) puts OpenAI near $70B run-rate and Anthropic about $65B in July, on different revenue bases.

By ticker. AMZN funder, cloud, channel: $18.0B funded, $110B owed. GOOGL: up to $40B, $111.1B owed. MSFT: up to $5B, $31.4B owed, $3.2B gain (Jul 29, T1). NVDA up to $10B. AMD up to $5B in, over $20B owed. AVGO $10B TPU order. Hosts: WULF $19B, RUM $13.7B, AKAM $11.6B, RIOT $9.1B, HUT $7.0B. Holders: CRM $3.0B (six months), ZM $1.6B (quarter) gains. SPCX $1.25B a month.

means.t: Each hyperscaler is funder, compute seller and channel; Google and Microsoft are also rivals. The equity buys economics without control: Amazon holds non-voting preferred and its notes convert to non-voting common on an IPO, subject to a cap (10-Q, T1). Holders book the mark. Amazon's Q1 gain was $16.8B pre-tax against $30.3B net income, priced by rounds where hyperscalers supplied $15B of Series H's $65B.

Circularity has two legs in the record: equity in from Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD, and compute out to the same names, AMD over $20B against up to $5B. Nvidia sits on both sides at Beacon Point: Lambda installs Nvidia GPUs for Anthropic while Nvidia pays Hut 8 rent (T3). No filing traces cash from an investment to a supplier invoice, so 'circular' is an inference.

Channels run in layers. Cloud marketplaces carried 47% of 2025 sales and kept about 16 cents a dollar, and The Information says Amazon takes roughly half the gross profit on Amazon-routed sales (T3). Anthropic books the sale gross as principal. Snowflake, Databricks and Salesforce bundle Claude. Services firms supply seats 'available to'. Cloud partners collect receivables too, 60% at end-2025 against 42% (Reuters, T3).

The share series measure four different things. Menlo surveyed usage, then estimated dollars. a16z surveyed production breadth. Ramp counts businesses with card spend. OpenRouter counts tokens. Anthropic leads on dollars and card adoption and trails on breadth. Its OpenRouter token share fell to 13.3% from 29.1% (T4). Menlo is an Anthropic investor and Anthropic repeats its 40%, so that figure is not independent.

implications.t: Reprice 'up to' as options. Count only filed dollars as raised: Amazon's $18.0B. Treat Google's $30B as target-gated and Microsoft's $5B, Nvidia's $10B and AMD's $5B as unfunded until a filing says otherwise. Keep four $15B items apart: the Microsoft and Nvidia cap, Series H's hyperscaler share, Amazon's facility and the pre-IPO revolver. Capital efficiency counts equity only, never debt.

Underwrite Amazon and Google as one counterparty on three lines: 47% of 2025 sales as channel, $221.1B as supplier, equity ceilings near $76B as investor. The draft prospectus warns of conflicts of interest with both (T3). Amazon and Google are paid shortfalls, while xAI can exit on 90 days' notice. Ask the S-1 for 2026 channel share and whether $150.0B of named neocloud deals sits above the $518B floor.

Chart shares by basis, never as one line. Tag each point survey, card spend or tokens, and mark Menlo as investor-published. Bulls can cite dollars and card adoption. Bears can cite breadth, 78% vs 44%, and token share. TechCrunch says OpenAI is gaining, but Ramp's May to July figures show Anthropic's lead widening from 2 to 4 points. June is missing.

Rank public exposure by the share of own size the record gives, then by dollars. RUM: contract over 3x market cap (T3). Riot: $9.1B of $9.8B contracted revenue. Amazon: $16.8B Q1 pre-tax gain vs $30.3B net income. Salesforce: 45% of strategic portfolio. Broadcom: $10B order is 13.7% of AI backlog. Then Akamai, TeraWulf, Zoom, Microsoft, Alphabet, AMD, Nvidia. No market caps are computed.

second_order: An IPO near the reported $2T, 2.07x Series H, re-marks every holder again: TheStreet puts Amazon's stake at $300B to $400B against $190.4B carried, and Amazon's notes convert to non-voting common on the IPO, subject to a cap (10-Q, T1). Sell-side must then separate Anthropic marks from AMZN, MSFT, CRM and ZM earnings. The gains recur each priced round, $9.5B in Q3 2025 and $16.8B in Q1 2026.

Nvidia as IPO anchor, up to $10B or about 0.5% at $2T (Reuters, T3), would put a chip supplier in the book while Akamai and RUM already issue Anthropic warrants. Equity then flows both ways between Anthropic and its suppliers. That extends the IPO absorption worry: the price-sensitive float is smaller than the $100B raise, but price discovery is less clean. Underwriters will face related-party questions.

Cursor, Claude's largest coding channel at ARR above $2B, moves under SpaceX in a $60.0B deal. SpaceX rents Anthropic compute on 90-day terms and competes through Grok. Anthropic cut off Windsurf (Jun 2025) and OpenAI (Aug 2025) to avoid supplying rivals. A cut-off would confirm the channel-risk thesis, though Cursor's share of AI-coding spend fell from 41% to about 26% on Ramp data (T3, low confidence).

Each host contract re-rates a small cap in a day: Akamai +17% after hours, Riot +25% after hours, TeraWulf above 10%, RUM +11.6%, while CoreWeave and Nebius fell 5% to 7% on RUM. The missing piece is concentration: Riot's Anthropic lease is 93% of its contracted revenue. If the IPO slips, these names carry the sharpest single-counterparty risk.

Anthropic's six closed deals carry no reported price above about $400M, and two lapsed talks at $6B and $7B sat 50% above Decart's $4B May valuation and 75% above the $4B MatX sought. A $2T stock currency changes the math. A priced deal above $1B would break the pattern and a Decart or MatX revival would reverse the walk-aways. Consensus may be assuming tuck-ins continue.

topics.house_view: (a) Extends: the market prices unlike quality alike, and Nscale's reported $30B to $35B IPO target rests on $140.6M of H1 revenue and a $1.02B H1 loss, priced off one Anthropic contract whose $44.6B value is press-reported and redacted in its S-1 exhibit. (b) Contradicts in size: marketplace fees were about $351M, 7.6% of FY2025 revenue (Reuters leak, T3), PitchBook sees a 6% to 10% cut from net presentation and The Information forecast 2026 payouts near one-tenth of revenue (both T3), all well below the desk's 39.75% haircut, so unless that haircut nets more than fees this slice does not support it, and Axios's $70B OpenAI against $65B Anthropic still mixes net and gross. (c) Extends: strategic holders are less price-sensitive than the $100B headline raise implies, since Nvidia is reported at up to $10B, Amazon's notes convert to non-voting common on an IPO and its $15.0B facility stays open for 30 months, yet the $2T ask is 2.07x the last mark. (d) Confirms with a wrinkle: $8.0B of Amazon's $18.0B entered as convertible notes, every 'up to' is unfunded, and the $15B revolver and $34.5B TPU SPV notes are debt, so only filed equity counts. (e) Confirms: seats, run-rate and contract value mean different things across software, cloud and hosting, since Deloitte's 470,000 is 'available to' and RUM's $13.7B is six-year contract value.
